lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 35

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Lie He Told
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun caught up within a dozen paces.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She did not run and she did not shout. She simply walked alongside him, her presence a weight he had not asked for and could not put down.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The corridor stretched ahead, narrow and oppressive. Torchlight died against the darkness before it could reach the walls.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek kept his eyes fixed forward.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You lied,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her voice contained no anger. That was worse. It was flat and clinical, the voice of someone examining a wound and deciding, with professional detachment, how deep it went and whether it would scar.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek kept walking.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I haven't said anything.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You read the journal. You closed it. You decided what the rest of us were allowed to know.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She placed each word carefully.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That is a lie of a different kind. You have never once refused to show me the words before.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stopped.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal was warm against his fingers when he pulled it free. The mark under the linen on his palm pulsed once, slow and deliberate, as if the account were taking notice of the intention itself.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He intended to open it. He intended to end the accusation with evidence.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not open it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun watched the decision form on his face.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You're still deciding,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Even now.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg's voice carried from ahead.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: If the two of you are going to stand there arguing about paper, the rest of us are moving.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo did not look back. She simply continued walking, the figurine turning once in her hand and then forgotten again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek returned the journal to the satchel. The weight of the decision settled differently this time—not the clean absence of a payment already made, but the heavier, unfinished pressure of a payment deferred.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They walked in silence until the corridor forked.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three identical passages opened ahead, each sloping downward at the same angle, each breathing with the same slow rhythm. The torchlight revealed nothing that distinguished one from the others.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stepped forward and studied the stone above each opening. When she began to copy one of the incomplete symbols, the mark on her parchment went blank under the stylus.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: They're the same,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Or the City wants us to believe they're the same.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo looked at the three openings with the remote attention she now gave anything that could not be priced.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Then we pick one and stop standing here.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg shook his head.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Last time we picked, the walls rearranged themselves behind us. I'd rather know which one is the trap.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: They're all traps,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The only question is which trap the City prefers us to choose.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek opened the journal.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The page that had been blank a moment earlier now held a single line in the hand that was neither his father's nor his own:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: THE LEFT PATH BELONGS TO THE ONE WHO WAS NEVER SENT.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He read it twice. The sentence did not say the path was safe. It did not say the path was dangerous. It only assigned ownership.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He closed the book before anyone else could see it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun was watching his face.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: What does it say?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He could have told her. He could have shown her the page. He could have treated the information as shared rather than private.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked at the three openings, at BAH-lahg waiting for direction, at En-HEH-doo already half-turned toward the left-hand passage because someone else would eventually declare one of them relevant.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He converted ownership into safety because safety was the word that would make the others follow.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It says the left path is safe.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stared at him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For a moment he thought she might argue, might reach for the journal again, might demand he open it and prove the accusation one way or the other.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then she simply looked away, and something in her posture folded inward, the way paper folds when it has finally given up resisting the crease.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek turned toward the left-hand passage.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not look back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind him Ninsun remained standing for a long moment before her footsteps finally started again—quieter now, more careful, as though she had learned something about the ground beneath her that she had not known before.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek reached the mouth of the left-hand passage and stopped because some remaining part of him expected Ninsun beside him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A heartbeat later he could not remember why he had stopped.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun was still there, a dozen paces behind him, her arms wrapped around herself against a cold that had nothing to do with temperature.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He knew her name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then he walked on.
